title: unreachable! in parse_header_typed match is structural smell
description: mime-tree/src/header_typed.rs:199-239 — parse_header_typed early-returns for HeaderForm::Raw at L199-L204, then falls into a match form { ... } at L238 where the Raw arm is HeaderForm::Raw => unreachable!("handled above"). The unreachable!() is guarded by an invariant verified two lines earlier, so it cannot actually trigger, but it is still production code that says 'I gave up structuring this cleanly'. Two idiomatic fixes: (a) handle Raw inside the match arm and compute the CRLF-normalized buf lazily only in the non-Raw arms; (b) make the early-return idiom explicit by lifting the body into a helper that returns Option<HeaderValueTyped> for Raw and unwraps cleanly. As written, a future hand adding a HeaderForm variant must remember to leave Raw at the top — the compiler cannot enforce that. Per the prompt's error-handling section: 'panic! or unreachable! where returning Err is feasible' applies indirectly here — restructuring eliminates the panic surface entirely.
close_reason: Code cleanup batch: (.3) removed dead 'year != 0' guard in date arm and replaced comment with accurate description of what month/day == 0 catches (year mapping in mail-parser-0.11 means parts[2] is never 0 after remap); (.21) eliminated unreachable! by folding Raw and URLs handling into the same outer match as the other forms — no top-level if-and-then-match anymore; (.22) replaced split_last + unwrap_or_else with straightforward slice arithmetic via a new crlf_terminated helper returning Cow; (.23) extracted trim_or_none helper for the RFC 8621 §4.1.2.3/§4.1.2.4 display-name normalisation rule, called from both convert_addr and group_addresses.
